title: Rate limit an API by user
tasks: rate limit an api by user

requirements.text: Each authenticated user (or API key) has an independent quota; one user's traffic never consumes another's
Requests within the configured limit and window are allowed, further requests are denied, and the quota refills or resets on schedule
Denied requests get 429 with Retry-After and rate-limit headers, without running the handler
Concurrent requests for one key never exceed the limit
Limiter state is bounded and idle keys expire
Counts are shared across server instances and survive restarts (for example Redis or the database)
The key comes from the authenticated identity on the server, never from client-controlled headers such as X-Forwarded-For

evidence.name: token bucket allows capacity, denies the next, and refills over injected time
fixed window allows limit per window and resets at the boundary
sliding window counts the trailing window exactly
rateLimitResponse builds a 429 with Retry-After and RateLimit headers
concurrent requests on the memory store never exceed the limit
memory store is bounded with LRU eviction and expires state

implementations.notes: Only the single-process memory store is implemented and tested; a shared store must implement the documented atomic update contract

evidence.name: token-bucket: vector sequence with injected clock

notes: Key derivation from the session is documented in the rate-limit CONTRACT.md but is the application's code; no shared (Redis/SQL) store ships.
